Q: Removing items from a players inventory A:

removeAll() will remove ALL the matching objects, based on the equals() method. So when you have same objects (according to equals()) in your list and use removeAll() with an object, that it "equal" to one of them, they all get deleted.

You can use remove(Object) to remove only one object which matches the given object based on the equals() method. See the documentation:

boolean remove(Object o)

Removes a single instance of the specified element from this collection, if it is present (optional operation). [...]

(emphasis mine)

A simple "foreach" loop will do:

for (Item item : toRemove) {
    inventory.remove(item);     // removes only one
    requiredItems.remove(item); // removes only one
}

Q: How to escape a $-sign in a dockerfile? A:

I found hints to use \$

Yes, that one is correct. This ($JAVA_OPTS → \$JAVA_OPTS) should work fine in terms of appending the content you specified to the file:

RUN echo "JAVA_OPTS=\$JAVA_OPTS -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=${CERT_DIR}/${HOSTNAME}_truststore.jks" >> ${BIN_DIR}/envvars
RUN echo "JAVA_OPTS=\$JAVA_OPTS -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=${PWD_TRUSTSTORE}" >> ${BIN_DIR}/envvars
RUN echo "export JAVA_OPTS" >> ${BIN_DIR}/envvars

In a RUN instruction, the only variable expansion is performed by the shell, and the Dockerfile-level escape character is only parsed at the end of the line, so only the shell’s escape character is relevant here. The backslash prevents variable expansion in a double-quoted string in any POSIX-compatible shell.

But assuming envvars is itself a script targeted at a POSIX-compatible shell, JAVA_OPTS=$JAVA_OPTS -Dfoo=bar will try to run -Dfoo=bar as a command; it’s missing a layer of quotes.

Here’s what I’d go for:

RUN printf >>${BIN_DIR}/envvars 'export JAVA_OPTS=${JAVA_OPTS:-}%q\n' "\
 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=${CERT_DIR}/${HOSTNAME}\
 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=$PWD_TRUSTSTORE"
  • single-quoted string for the literal ${JAVA_OPTS:-} to avoid escaping entirely
  • one layer instead of three (fun fact: building up a file one line at a time in Docker like this takes quadratic space and time!)
  • works even if the immediately-expanded variables contain shell metacharacters (including $, \, ', etc., but not whitespace), depending on how $JAVA_OPTS is used – some tools use java $JAVA_OPTS, and others use eval "java $JAVA_OPTS" (this is targeted at the former; for the latter, you need another layer of %q, and whitespace will work then)

It does require a printf that supports %q, so combine it with a SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-eu", "-c"] directive.

Or, if you don’t care what metacharacters in the build’s environment variables might do to the script, you can skip the RUN shell entirely and use COPY with a heredoc:

COPY <<EOF ${BIN_DIR}/envvars
export JAVA_OPTS="\${JAVA_OPTS:-}\\
 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=${CERT_DIR}/${HOSTNAME}\\
 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=$PWD_TRUSTSTORE\\
"
EOF

This one does use the Dockerfile-level escape character.

Q: org.mockito.exceptions.misusing.WrongTypeOfReturnValue: A:

Changes to be made:

  1. thenReturn(Optional.of(ticket));

The argument inside thenReturn because of Optional.of() cannot be null. Instead use Optional.ofNullable(T value). Returns an Optional describing the specified value, if non-null, otherwise returns an empty.

  1. Change when(ticketService.findById(ticket.getId())).thenReturn(ticket); to doReturn(ticket).when(ticketService).findById(ticket.getId())

Read This: https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!topic/mockito/9WUvkhZUy90
